question: In which year did the ‘Battle of Buxar’ take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1764 CE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764 between the forces of the British East India Company, led by Major Hector Munro, and the combined armies of Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) and Shah Alam II (Mughal Emperor). (बक्सर का युद्ध — 1764)

• The British victory made them the real masters of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The battle led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), under which Shah Alam II granted the Diwani rights (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha to the East India Company — the beginning of the Dual Government in Bengal introduced by Robert Clive.

• 1757 — Battle of Plassey (Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daula).

• 1761 — Third Battle of Panipat (Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas).

NOTE

• Buxar is situated in present-day Bihar, on the bank of the Ganga.

• Plassey gave the British political influence in Bengal; Buxar gave them legal and military supremacy over northern India.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mandates that the state should protect every monument or place of artistic or historic interest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 49.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 49 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP), states that it shall be the obligation of the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest declared to be of national importance from spoliation, disfigurement, destruction, removal, disposal or export. (अनुच्छेद 49 — स्मारकों का संरक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 39A — Equal justice and free legal aid.

• Article 48A — Protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976).

• Article 50 — Separation of the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

NOTE

• DPSPs are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution and are borrowed from the Irish Constitution. They are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country.

• The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), founded in 1861 by Alexander Cunningham, is the nodal agency for protecting monuments of national importance.

question: To mark the celebration of Gandhi Jayanti, the _____________ celebrates it as International Day of Non-Violence.
option_3: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Nations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The United Nations General Assembly, by a resolution of 15 June 2007, declared 2 October — the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi — as the International Day of Non-Violence. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अहिंसा दिवस — 2 अक्टूबर)

• The day reaffirms "the universal relevance of the principle of non-violence" and the desire "to secure a culture of peace, tolerance, understanding and non-violence".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mahatma Gandhi (2 October 1869 – 30 January 1948) was born at Porbandar, Gujarat; his philosophy rested on Satya (truth), Ahimsa (non-violence) and Satyagraha.

• India also observes 30 January as Martyrs' Day (Shaheed Diwas).

NOTE

• Other UN days proposed by India: International Day of Yoga (21 June) and International Year of Millets (2023).

• The UN was founded on 24 October 1945; its headquarters are in New York, and it currently has 193 member states.

question: Alarmel Valli is a __________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alarmel Valli is a world-renowned exponent of Bharatanatyam, the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu. She is known for the Pandanallur style and has been honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2004) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1991). (अलरमेल वल्ली — भरतनाट्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; derived from the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni; other exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Malavika Sarukkai.

• Odissi — Odisha (Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh).

• Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh (Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy).

• Kathak — Uttar Pradesh (Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: Which of the following is an example of a microfinance institution (MFI) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bandhan Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bandhan began in 2001 at Kolkata as a microfinance institution (MFI) founded by Chandra Shekhar Ghosh, providing small collateral-free loans mainly to women in rural areas. It received a universal banking licence from the RBI in 2014 and started operations as Bandhan Bank in August 2015. (माइक्रोफाइनेंस संस्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Microfinance provides small-value financial services — credit, savings, insurance — to low-income households that lack access to formal banking.

• SBI, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank are commercial banks (SBI is a public sector bank; ICICI and HDFC are private sector banks), not MFIs.

• Other Indian MFIs: Bharat Financial Inclusion (SKS), Ujjivan, Equitas, Spandana Sphoorty.

NOTE

• The microfinance movement was pioneered by Prof. Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh through the Grameen Bank; he won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

• In India, SIDBI and NABARD support microfinance; the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD in 1992.

question: Which of the following is an autobiography by Mahatma Gandhi?
option_1: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Story of My Experiments with Truth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Story of My Experiments with Truth" is the autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi. It was written in Gujarati and published in weekly instalments in the journal Navjivan between 1925 and 1929; the English translation was done by Mahadev Desai. (सत्य के साथ मेरे प्रयोग)

• It covers Gandhi's life from childhood up to 1921.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "My Truth" — autobiography of Indira Gandhi.

• "Matters of Discretion" — autobiography of Inder Kumar Gujral, former Prime Minister of India.

• "My Country My Life" — autobiography of L. K. Advani.

NOTE

• Other famous autobiographies: An Autobiography / Toward Freedom (Jawaharlal Nehru), Wings of Fire (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh), Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), Unbreakable (Mary Kom).

question: Which of the following has initiated the Village Defence Guards scheme to instil a sense of self protection and ensure the safety and security of villages and infrastructural installations in and around the villages?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Village Defence Guards Scheme (VDGS), 2022 was approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. Its aim is to instil a sense of self-protection among villagers and to ensure the safety and security of villages and infrastructural installations in and around them, especially in vulnerable border and hilly districts. (ग्राम रक्षा गार्ड योजना — जम्मू-कश्मीर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme replaced the earlier Village Defence Committees (VDCs), first set up in the mid-1990s in the Jammu region to counter militancy.

• Members are volunteers who are armed and paid a monthly honorarium; those leading a group receive a higher amount.

• They function under the supervision of the local Superintendent of Police (SP).

NOTE

• Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory with a legislature on 31 October 2019 after the abrogation of Article 370, while Ladakh became a UT without a legislature.

question: The Sirpur Shrine is situated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sirpur is an ancient heritage site on the bank of the river Mahanadi in the Mahasamund district of Chhattisgarh. It is famous for the Lakshmana Temple, one of India's oldest brick temples (7th century CE), along with Buddhist viharas, Jain shrines and Shaiva monuments. (सिरपुर — छत्तीसगढ़)

• Sirpur was the capital of the Sarabhapuriya and later the Panduvamshi (Somavamshi) rulers of Dakshina Kosala.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) is believed to have visited Sirpur in the 7th century CE.

• Other important sites of Chhattisgarh: Bhoramdeo Temple, Chitrakote Falls (the "Niagara of India"), Rajim, Kanger Valley National Park, Indravati National Park.

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000; its capital is Raipur (with the planned city Naya Raipur/Atal Nagar).

question: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the climate of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Longitude.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Longitude does not affect climate. Longitudes are used to determine time (local and standard time), not temperature or rainfall. India's standard time is fixed by the 82°30'E meridian passing through Mirzapur (Uttar Pradesh). (देशांतर — जलवायु को प्रभावित नहीं करता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Latitude affects climate strongly: the Tropic of Cancer (23½°N) divides India, so the south has a tropical climate and the north a subtropical/temperate one.

• Altitude affects climate because temperature falls with height (normal lapse rate ≈ 6.5°C per 1,000 m); hence hill stations such as Shimla are cooler than the plains.

• Winds, especially the South-West monsoon and the North-East (retreating) monsoon, control India's rainfall pattern.

NOTE

• Other controls of India's climate: distance from the sea (continentality), relief features such as the Himalayas and the Western Ghats, ocean currents, upper air circulation (jet streams) and El Niño/La Niña.

• The Himalayas block the cold Central Asian winds, keeping India warmer than places at the same latitude.

question: What is the common name for a saturated solution of calcium hydroxide widely used as a raw material in the chemical industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Slaked lime.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂, is commonly called slaked lime (its solution in water is known as lime water). It is a widely used raw material in the chemical industry — in bleaching powder manufacture, water treatment, whitewashing, mortar and plaster, and for neutralising acidic soil. (चूने का पानी / बुझा हुआ चूना)

• It is obtained when quicklime (CaO) reacts vigorously with water:

◦ CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + heat (this reaction is called slaking of lime).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Calomel is mercurous chloride (Hg₂Cl₂), used in the calomel electrode.

• Burnt lime / quicklime is calcium oxide (CaO), obtained by heating limestone.

• Limestone is calcium carbonate (CaCO₃); on heating it decomposes: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.

NOTE

• Lime water turns milky when carbon dioxide is passed through it, because insoluble calcium carbonate is formed — the standard laboratory test for CO₂.

• Bleaching powder: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.

question: Who among the following singers is from Andhra Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is S Janaki.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• S. Janaki (Sistla Janaki), popularly called the Nightingale of South India, was born at Pallapatla in the Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh in 1938. She has recorded over 48,000 songs in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Hindi and other languages and has won four National Film Awards. (एस. जानकी — आंध्र प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Usha Uthup was born in Mumbai (Maharashtra) and is famous for her distinctive deep voice; she was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2024.

• Asha Bhosle was born at Sangli, Maharashtra; she holds a Guinness record for the most recorded songs and received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2000).

• Alka Yagnik was born in Kolkata, West Bengal.

NOTE

• Other legendary playback singers of the South: S. P. Balasubrahmanyam (Andhra Pradesh, Padma Vibhushan, six National Awards), K. J. Yesudas (Kerala), P. Susheela (Andhra Pradesh).

question: Who led the Congress in the second round table conference held in London?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Second Round Table Conference was held in London from September to December 1931. Mahatma Gandhi attended it as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress, following the Gandhi–Irwin Pact of March 1931. (द्वितीय गोलमेज सम्मेलन — महात्मा गांधी)

• The conference failed, chiefly over the question of separate electorates for the minorities, especially the Depressed Classes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sarojini Naidu, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Pandit Nehru's associates were present in other capacities; Sarojini Naidu accompanied Gandhi as a representative of Indian women.

• First Round Table Conference (Nov 1930 – Jan 1931) — boycotted by the Congress.

• Third Round Table Conference (Nov – Dec 1932) — the Congress again did not participate.

NOTE

• After the failure of the second conference, Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award (Aug 1932), which was modified by the Poona Pact (Sept 1932) between Gandhi and Dr B. R. Ambedkar.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which state has the second highest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, among the states, Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1084 females per 1000 males) and Tamil Nadu has the second highest (996), followed by Andhra Pradesh (993). (तमिलनाडु — दूसरा सर्वाधिक लिंगानुपात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sex ratio = number of females per 1000 males.

• India's overall sex ratio in 2011 was 943, up from 933 in 2001.

• Among Union Territories, Puducherry (1037) had the highest sex ratio and Daman & Diu (618) the lowest.

• Haryana (879) had the lowest sex ratio among the states.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence.

• Other 2011 figures: total population 121.08 crore; literacy rate 74.04%; Kerala most literate (93.91%) and Bihar least literate (61.8%); density 382 persons/km².

question: Factor cost is also known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is input cost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Factor cost is the cost of all the factors of production — land (rent), labour (wages), capital (interest) and entrepreneurship (profit) — used in producing a good or service. It is therefore also called the input cost. (साधन लागत = आगत लागत)

• It excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Relationship: Market Price = Factor Cost + Indirect Taxes − Subsidies.

• Hence GDP at market price = GDP at factor cost + Indirect taxes − Subsidies.

• From 2015, India shifted to measuring national income at market prices with 2011-12 as the base year, and uses Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices.

NOTE

• Factors of production and their rewards: Land → Rent, Labour → Wages, Capital → Interest, Entrepreneur → Profit.

• NNP at factor cost = National Income.

question: Which cell found in the bone marrow acts as a repair system for the body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stem cells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Stem cells present in the bone marrow are undifferentiated cells that can divide indefinitely and differentiate into many specialised cell types. They therefore act as an internal repair system, replacing worn-out or damaged cells throughout life. (स्टेम कोशिकाएँ — शरीर की मरम्मत प्रणाली)

• Haematopoietic stem cells of the bone marrow produce red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bone cells (osteoblasts, osteocytes, osteoclasts) build and maintain the bone matrix but do not act as a general repair system.

• Fat cells (adipocytes) store energy as fat.

• Muscle cells (myocytes) bring about contraction and movement.

NOTE

• Bone marrow transplantation is used to treat leukaemia, thalassemia and aplastic anaemia.

• Stem cells are of two broad types: embryonic (pluripotent) and adult/somatic (multipotent). Umbilical cord blood is a rich source of stem cells.

question: Which of the following is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kalbelia is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by the women of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community. The dancers wear flowing black ghagras and move in a serpentine manner to the music of the been (pungi) and khanjari. It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010. (कालबेलिया — राजस्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chang Lo (Sua Lua) — folk dance of the Chang tribe of Nagaland, performed to celebrate victory in war.

• Daskathia and Pala Jatra — traditional ballad/folk performance forms of Odisha.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Ghoomar, Chari, Kachchhi Ghodi, Bhavai, Terah Taali, Gair, Kathputli.

• Folk dances elsewhere: Bihu (Assam), Garba (Gujarat), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Lavani (Maharashtra), Chhau (Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal), Rouf (Jammu & Kashmir).

question: When was the first general election for Lok Sabha held in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1951-52.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first general election to the Lok Sabha was held from 25 October 1951 to 21 February 1952. It was conducted in 68 phases and about 17.32 crore voters were eligible. (प्रथम आम चुनाव — 1951-52)

• The Indian National Congress won 364 of the 489 seats, and Jawaharlal Nehru became the first elected Prime Minister of independent India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The election was supervised by Sukumar Sen, India's first Chief Election Commissioner.

• The Election Commission of India was constituted on 25 January 1950; that date is now observed as National Voters' Day.

• Voting age was 21 years; it was lowered to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

NOTE

• The Lok Sabha's maximum strength is 550 elected members (530 from states + 20 from UTs) under Article 81; its normal term is five years.

• Elections are held on the basis of universal adult franchise (Article 326).

question: Who among the following female singers has been felicitated with the Bharat Ratna?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lata Mangeshkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022), the "Nightingale of India", was conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2001 — India's highest civilian award. She recorded songs in 36 Indian languages over a career of more than seven decades. (लता मंगेशकर — भारत रत्न, 2001)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other honours won by her: Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989), Padma Bhushan (1969), Padma Vibhushan (1999) and the Legion of Honour of France (2007).

• Asha Bhosle (her sister) received the Padma Vibhushan (2008) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2000) — but not the Bharat Ratna.

• Vani Jayaram was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2023; Usha Uthup received the Padma Bhushan in 2024.

NOTE

• Musicians awarded the Bharat Ratna: M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Ravi Shankar (1999), Lata Mangeshkar (2001), Bismillah Khan (2001), Bhupen Hazarika (2019, posthumous).

• The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954; the first woman to receive it was Indira Gandhi (1971).

question: Which of the following states of India is the first to receive rainfall from the South West Monsoon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The South-West Monsoon normally strikes the Kerala coast around 1 June each year, making Kerala the first state of India to receive monsoon rainfall. This is called the "onset (burst) of the monsoon". (केरल — मानसून का आगमन, 1 जून)

• Before Kerala, the monsoon first reaches the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (around 20 May), but that is a Union Territory, not a state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The South-West Monsoon splits into two branches — the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch.

• The monsoon covers the whole country by about 15 July and begins retreating from north-west India in early September.

• India receives about 75% of its annual rainfall from the South-West Monsoon (June–September).

NOTE

• Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Sohra) in Meghalaya receive the highest rainfall in the world.

• Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain from the North-East (retreating) monsoon (October–December).

• The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD), established in 1875, issues monsoon forecasts.

question: Which famous Indian danseuse became the first woman to be nominated as a member of Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904–1986), the celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer and revivalist, became the first woman to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 1952. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल — राज्यसभा में मनोनीत पहली महिला)

• She founded Kalakshetra at Chennai in 1936 to revive and teach classical dance and music, and worked to restore social respectability to Bharatanatyam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She was also a noted animal-welfare activist and piloted the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960; she was the first chairperson of the Animal Welfare Board of India.

• She was offered the post of President of India in 1977 but declined it.

• Sitara Devi was a famous Kathak dancer; Mrinalini Sarabhai was a Bharatanatyam and Kathakali exponent who founded Darpana Academy, Ahmedabad.

NOTE

• Under Article 80, the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

question: Which of the following is a famous novel written by Munshi Premchand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Godan" (1936) is the most famous novel of Munshi Premchand (pen name of Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, 1880–1936). It portrays the exploitation and tragedy of the Indian peasant through the story of Hori Mahato and his lifelong desire to own a cow. (गोदान — मुंशी प्रेमचंद)

• Premchand is regarded as the greatest writer of Hindi–Urdu fiction and is called "Upanyas Samrat" (Emperor of Novels).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Gunaho Ka Devta" — by Dharamvir Bharati.

• "Kitne Pakistan" — by Kamleshwar (Sahitya Akademi Award, 2003).

• "Rag Darbari" — by Shrilal Shukla (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1969).

NOTE

• Other works of Premchand: Sevasadan, Rangbhoomi, Karmabhoomi, Nirmala, Gaban, Kafan, Idgah, Panch Parmeshwar, Poos Ki Raat, Shatranj Ke Khiladi.

• His first collection, Soz-e-Watan (1908), was banned by the British.

question: India played in the finals of the 2023 World Test Championship against Australia. Where was this match conducted?
solution_text:
The correct answer is London.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC World Test Championship (WTC) Final 2023 was played between India and Australia from 7 to 11 June 2023 at The Oval, London (England). Australia won by 209 runs to become the WTC champions. (लंदन — द ओवल)

• Travis Head (163 runs) was adjudged Player of the Match.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first WTC Final (2021) was played at the Ageas Bowl, Southampton, where New Zealand beat India by 8 wickets.

• The WTC 2023-25 Final was scheduled at Lord's, London.

• The ICC (International Cricket Council) has its headquarters at Dubai, UAE.

NOTE

• India's Test captain in the 2023 final was Rohit Sharma; Australia was led by Pat Cummins.

• The World Test Championship was launched in 2019 to give context to bilateral Test cricket.

question: D Gukesh was awarded player of the year award in March 2023. He plays which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dommaraju Gukesh (D. Gukesh) is an Indian chess Grandmaster from Chennai, Tamil Nadu. In March 2023 he was named the ChessBase India Player of the Year. (डी. गुकेश — शतरंज)

• He became a Grandmaster in 2019 at the age of 12 years, 7 months and 17 days, making him one of the youngest GMs in history.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In 2023, Gukesh overtook Viswanathan Anand to become India's highest-rated chess player, ending Anand's 36-year reign at the top.

• He was part of the Indian team that won bronze at the 44th Chess Olympiad (Chennai, 2022), where he won an individual gold on board one.

• He later won the Candidates Tournament 2024 and became the youngest ever World Chess Champion (2024).

NOTE

• Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster (1988) and a five-time World Champion.

• Chess is governed internationally by FIDE; India's other top players include R. Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi and Koneru Humpy.

question: According to the Ministry of Textile 2022-23, which state is the second largest producer of cotton?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Ministry of Textiles (2022-23) data, Gujarat is the largest producer of cotton in India and Maharashtra is the second largest, followed by Telangana. (महाराष्ट्र — कपास का दूसरा सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक)

• Cotton is a kharif crop and is known as "White Gold".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Cotton requires high temperature (21–30°C), light rainfall (50–100 cm), 210 frost-free days and bright sunshine; the black regur soil of the Deccan plateau is ideal for it.

• India is the largest producer of cotton in the world and also the largest area under cotton cultivation.

• Major cotton-growing states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab.

NOTE

• Bt cotton, a genetically modified variety, was approved in India in 2002 and is the only GM crop permitted for commercial cultivation.

• The Cotton Corporation of India (CCI), set up in 1970, undertakes Minimum Support Price (MSP) operations for cotton.

question: In which of the following States was the final of the 2023 Intercontinental Cup football championship held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2023 Intercontinental Cup football tournament was held at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar, Odisha, from 9 to 18 June 2023. In the final, India beat Lebanon 2–0, with Sunil Chhetri scoring both goals. (ओडिशा — कलिंग स्टेडियम, भुवनेश्वर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The four teams in the 2023 edition were India, Lebanon, Mongolia and Vanuatu.

• India also won the 2018 Intercontinental Cup (held in Mumbai) and the SAFF Championship 2023 in the same year; India's coach was Igor Stimac.

• Sunil Chhetri is India's highest goal-scorer and among the top international scorers among active players.

NOTE

• Odisha has become a major sports hub, hosting the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup (2018 and 2023) at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar and the Birsa Munda Hockey Stadium, Rourkela.

• Indian football is governed by the All India Football Federation (AIFF), founded in 1937.
